key_insight: Omnitree forests enable axis-selective mesh adaptation with provably output-optimal work and a split-order-independent description of representable partitions.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports anisotropic high-order finite elements and multigrid hierarchies for resolving moving layers in space–time and parameter-dependent simulations.
method: Represent partitions canonically, independently of cell-splitting order.
Prove work bounds for refinement, coarsening, face balancing and selected coarse-mesh construction.
Use polynomial trace equations for conformity and reconstruction moments for interpolation-error bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical complexity and approximation results, plus moving heat-layer resolution with polynomial degrees up to four on unstructured 4D space–time and 5D space–time–parameter meshes.
watch_item: Linear-work guarantees assume fixed dimension and key width; crossed-face conformity and logarithmic interpolation losses require care in implementation.
paper_title: Forests of Omnitrees: Analysis and Applications to Anisotropic Space--Time Finite Elements
